investigations.question: Can a node whose configuration was left stale by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay actually win an election with fewer votes than a majority of the configuration recorded in its own committed log, while the remaining voters elect their own leader?
investigations.hypothesis: With the restarted node holding {A,B,C} while its log records the committed {A,B,C,D,E}, isolating it with one voter of the stale set lets it collect two votes (itself plus that voter) against its stale quorum of two and become leader, while the three remaining voters, who hold the current configuration, elect a second leader; both then accept commands.
investigations.discriminator: One cluster whose only difference is the defect: node A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change beyond its snapshot, then a partition separates A and one stale voter from the other three. Predicted difference against a control restart of the same node without RestoreCommittedLogs (or with a refreshed snapshot): the feature-on node reaches Leader with two votes; the control stays follower/candidate because its quorum is three.

investigations.question: Which permitted mechanism reconciles the divergent entries and applied state left by the stale-configuration split: does the library engage installSnapshot, log compaction or a user restore on its own once the cluster is whole, or does the divergence persist while the node participates normally?
investigations.hypothesis: Nothing in the ordinary AppendEntries path reconciles same-term conflicts, and the stale node keeps serving and replicating, so it never falls far enough behind for the leader to send a snapshot; only an explicit snapshot install (forced by compaction plus a lagging follower), a user Restore or a truncation caused by a different term would replace the divergent entry and FSM state.
investigations.discriminator: After the healed split state, force the surviving leader to snapshot and compact past the follower's nextIndex and append one more entry, then sample the divergent index and the applied commands on both sides. Predicted: without intervention the divergence persists, while a snapshot install replaces the restarted node's entry and FSM state with the leader's.

knowledge.statement: On a follower that receives an InstallSnapshot, the handler streams and finalises the snapshot, restores the FSM through fsmMutateCh, sets lastApplied and the last snapshot to the request's last log index and term, and replaces the latest and committed configuration from the request; the local log is then either removed entirely (monotonic stores) or compacted up to the snapshot index. A follower that has fallen behind a leader whose log was compacted is therefore sent a snapshot and ends up with the leader's FSM state, entry suffix and configuration, replacing any divergent entry it held at an index the leader also used.
knowledge.conditions: Triggered either because the leader can no longer serve the entries the follower needs (its log was compacted past the follower's position) or because the leader consumed a snapshot through the Restore contract and pushed it to its followers; observed with in-memory stores in both cases.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot loop treats a failed snapshot creation as a logged error and keeps running: when takeSnapshot returns an error other than ErrNothingNewToSnapshot the loop logs it and continues, so a node whose snapshot store keeps failing retains its last successful snapshot and its log grows without bound relative to it.
knowledge.conditions: Running leader or follower with a caller-provided SnapshotStore whose Create fails; observed through a wrapper store whose Create fails after the node's first snapshot, with four failed attempts while thousands of entries were committed.

knowledge.statement: A candidate is granted votes only if its log is at least as up to date as the voter's: requestVote rejects a candidate whose last log term is lower, or whose last log index is smaller at the same term. Consequently, once an entry at an index has been committed in term T by a leader whose log was the most up to date, any later leader must have a log whose last entry is at least as up to date, so it can only append entries beyond that index and cannot replace the entry at it with a different term; the entry can only be replaced by a snapshot install or a user restore.
knowledge.conditions: Voter-side vote admission (raft.go 1725-1750) applied to the split-brain state of this defect, where the conflicting entries are at the highest index of every log and at the same term.

knowledge.statement: The repository's own tests for Config.RestoreCommittedLogs exercise a single-node cluster that commits commands, takes a snapshot and restarts the node, asserting only that the FSM is replayed up to the log store's commit index and that the commit index sits between the snapshot index and the last log index; no test constructs a restart whose snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, and none observes the configuration or quorum the restarted node uses. The user-restore path is covered by snapshotAndRestore, which opens a snapshot, calls Restore on the leader and asserts that the FSM contents are reverted and that all nodes agree.
knowledge.conditions: Read of the target's test sources in the captured snapshot; test expectations describe the scenarios those tests construct, not the library's full contract.

knowledge.statement: The network transport routes an AppendEntries request to the heartbeat handler in its own goroutine only when the decoded request has a non-zero term, a leader address, zero PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm, no entries and a zero LeaderCommitIndex; every other AppendEntries request is dispatched to the Raft main loop. The handler accepts only AppendEntries commands and returns immediately when the node is shutting down, so the off-main-loop path cannot append entries or apply committed entries for the follower.
knowledge.conditions: NetworkTransport RPC decoding and dispatch; the equivalent InmemTransport does not implement the fast path (its SetHeartbeatHandler is a no-op), so this applies to the network transport only.

knowledge.statement: Vote admission treats an empty configuration as a bootstrap-style free pass: requestVote skips the membership guard whenever r.configurations.latest.Servers is empty, so a node whose live configuration is empty grants a vote to a candidate that is absent from the configuration recorded in its own committed log, provided the request's term is not older than the node's, the candidate's last log entry is at least as up to date and the node knows no leader.
knowledge.conditions: The receiver's in-memory latest configuration is empty while its log still records a committed configuration, as produced by a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose snapshot and scan start sit above the configuration entry; the vote request carries an ID and an at-least-as-up-to-date last log entry; the receiver knows no leader and the request's term is not older than its current term.

knowledge.statement: Both vote admission handlers skip their membership guard when the receiver's live configuration is empty: requestVote checks inConfiguration only when r.configurations.latest.Servers is non-empty, and requestPreVote repeats the same conditional check (and the same conditional hasVote check) before the leader and log up-to-dateness tests, so a node holding an empty configuration grants a pre-vote as well as a vote to a candidate the configuration recorded in its own log excludes.
knowledge.conditions: The receiver's in-memory latest configuration is empty while its log still records a committed configuration, as produced by a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose snapshot and scan start sit above the configuration entry; the request carries an ID and an at-least-as-up-to-date last log entry; the receiver knows no leader and the request's term is not older than its current term.

knowledge.statement: The AppendEntries handler never checks the sender against the configuration: after rejecting only terms older than its own it steps down if needed, adopts the request's address and ID as its leader, and proceeds to the log checks, so a follower accepts entries from any sender whose term is current regardless of whether that sender appears in the receiver's configuration or in the configuration recorded in its log.
knowledge.conditions: An AppendEntries request whose term is not older than the receiver's current term; the receiver holds no configuration entry naming the sender, as when its live configuration is empty or stale relative to its own committed log; the receiver is a follower or steps down on the request.

scope.description: Restart-shaped construction of a single node (LocalID A, ProtocolVersion 3, in-memory log/stable/snapshot stores) whose last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, observed with RestoreCommittedLogs off, on (construction only), and on with background goroutines started.

The FSM discards applied entries and its Restore accepts the snapshot bytes; snapshot restore therefore succeeds and lastApplied after restore is the snapshot index.
For the two construction cases conf.skipStartup is true, so no background goroutine runs and r.configurations is read directly as the state NewRaft computed.

For the live case the node runs normally (default timeouts) with no reachable peers, and the sample is taken only after the node has entered the candidate loop; the public GetConfiguration copy is read instead of r.configurations.

The snapshot was produced by the harness rather than by a live Snapshot() call, so the fixture's log/snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: For each mode the harness creates a fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots); it writes a version-1 snapshot at index 5, term 1 with configuration {A,B,C} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; it stores log entries 1=LogConfiguration{A,B,C}, 2..5=LogNoop, 6=LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, 7=LogNoop; it calls logs.StageCommitIndex(7). It then emits a 'fixture' event describing those stored facts, builds Config with DefaultConfig(), LocalID "A", a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs set from the mode, and calls NewRaft(conf, fsm, logs, stable, snaps, trans). In the two construction modes conf.skipStartup is left true, and a 'construct' event reports lastApplied, commit index, latest/committed configuration id sets and indexes, quorumSize, hasVote(self), the number of batches queued on fsmMutateCh and the number of FSM restores. In the live mode the background goroutines run; a 'live' event reports the public GetConfiguration id set, the node state and current term. Modes run in the order baseline, restore_committed, restore_committed_skip_startup_false so the emitted event order is fixture, construct, fixture, construct, fixture, live.

before.description: Restart-shaped construction of a single node (LocalID A, ProtocolVersion 3, in-memory log/stable/snapshot stores) whose last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry, observed with RestoreCommittedLogs off, on (construction only), and on with background goroutines started.

For the two construction cases conf.skipStartup is true, so no background goroutine runs and r.configurations is read directly as the state NewRaft computed.

For the live case the node runs normally (default timeouts) with no reachable peers, and the sample is taken only after the node has entered the candidate loop; the public GetConfiguration copy is read instead of r.configurations.
excluded: The election/quorum consequence is not executed here: no election with a majority of the current configuration and a minority of a stale one is run.
The snapshot was produced by the harness rather than by a live Snapshot() call, so the fixture's log/snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced.
No repository test was executed.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster (A..E, ProtocolVersion 3, default timeouts scaled to 50ms) whose node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change that is newer than A's last snapshot, then partitioned into {A,C} and {B,D,E}; every node of this deployment runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled so the commit index that the restart reads is the one the running protocol staged.
assumptions: Cluster state is produced through normal operations: BootstrapCluster({A,B,C}) from A, election, three committed applies, a user-triggered Snapshot on A, AddVoter(D) and AddVoter(E), and one further committed apply; no log entry, snapshot or index is written by the harness.

A is shut down (graceful Shutdown) rather than crashed, and its store objects (log store, stable store, snapshot store) are reused for the restart; the in-memory transports are reconnected so that the restarted A can reach only C.
The partition is expressed only by transport disconnection in both directions; the Raft fault model, RPC lifecycles and election timing are untouched.

All five nodes run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled from the start, which is the deployment mode whose restart behaviour is under test; the harness also records that disabling it during the first life leaves the stored commit index at 0.
The cluster is stopped at the end of the test; the observation window uses the nodes' own election timeouts plus a bounded wait for both partitions to elect.
excluded: No process crash or storage fault is injected: A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact.
No on-disk log store is exercised; only the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore.
The conflicting commits are observed at the two leaders; the loss of the minority entry after healing is not executed.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five InmemTransports with addresses A..E, a full mesh of connections, and per node an InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots). It calls BootstrapCluster(confA, logsA, stableA, snapsA, transA, {A,B,C}), then NewRaft for A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true; it waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if another node won, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A (snapshot index 6, configuration {A,B,C}). It then starts D and E with empty stores and calls AddVoter on the leader for each of them, followed by one more applied command so every follower stages a commit index at or above the new configuration entry (index 8). It emits a 'fixture' event with the snapshot index, the newest configuration entry index and membership, the stored commit index, the pre-restart configuration A reports and the derived operands commit_covers_config_entry and snapshot_before_config_entry. It shuts A down, cuts the transports so that {A,C} cannot reach {B,D,E}, creates a fresh transport for A connected only to C, and restarts A from its own stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, emitting a 'restart' event with A's state, last applied index and reported configuration. It then waits for a leader in each partition and emits an 'outcome' event with the leaders and terms per partition, the leader count, whether each node in the minority partition is leader, the configurations reported by the restarted A, by C and by the majority leader, the result of an Apply submitted to each leader, the index and term each committed at, the two committed payloads and a derived conflicting_commits operand. Event order: fixture, restart, outcome.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft NewRaft configuration scan combined with the RestoreCommittedLogs replay: the restarted node is responsible for deriving candidate admission and election quorum from the latest configuration entry in its own log, and voters are responsible for granting at most the votes their own view of the configuration requires.

comparisons.description: The restarted node's live configuration should be the membership of the committed configuration entry in its own log; this is the same predicate the earlier supplied-fixture experiment declared, here with stores produced by real operations.
A node whose effective configuration holds two of the five voters of the configuration recorded in its own committed log must not reach Leader while it can reach only one of those voters.
The cluster should have at most one leader; both partitions observed here are disjoint halves of one cluster.
Two leaders must not commit different entries at the same index and term.
A leader holding only a minority of the current voter set must not be able to commit an entry.
In-partition control: node C, whose configuration is the current one, must not become leader in the same two-voter partition.

semantic_changes: After the outcome sample the harness reconnects every transport pair, waits up to 15s for exactly one leader, applies one further entry on that leader and waits 300ms.

Three comparisons are added on the 'healed' event: entry payloads at the conflicting index must be consistent, the restarted node must report the committed membership after the cluster runs on, and its log must have advanced.

scope.description: A single node (LocalID A) constructed in two modes from the same in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} and a log of 9000 committed LogCommand entries above it (indices 1001..10000), with the commit-tracking store reporting commit index 10000; RestoreCommittedLogs off versus on, with normal initialization in both cases.
assumptions: The fixture is supplied by the harness (snapshot, 9000 entries, staged commit index); it is the restart-shaped state a node running with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the log entries by the store contract.

The number of batches the replay produces is derived from MaxAppendEntries (64) and the entries above the snapshot (9000), giving 141 batches, and is emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.
Non-return is evaluated by constructing in a goroutine and waiting 5s; the control uses the identical fixture with the feature off, so a slow fixture, slow store or slow FSM is excluded as the cause.
The feature-on node that never returns cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store is exercised; the in-memory CommitTrackingLogStore is used.
The blocked constructor is not resumed, so no recovery path after the stall is observed.
No repository test was executed.

basis.prefix: The harness builds fresh InmemTransport("A"), InmemStore (stable), InmemCommitTrackingStore (logs) and InmemSnapshotStore (snapshots) per mode; writes a version-1 snapshot at index 1000, term 1 with configuration {A} at configuration index 1 and closes the sink; stores 9000 LogCommand entries at indices 1001..10000 in batches of 256; and calls logs.StageCommitIndex(10000). It emits a 'fixture' event with the fixture operands (snapshot index, log last index, stored commit index, entries above the snapshot, MaxAppendEntries, batches required, observation window), then builds Config from DefaultConfig() with LocalID "A", a null logger and RestoreCommittedLogs set from the mode, and calls NewRaft(conf, probeFSM, logs, stable, snaps, trans) in a goroutine. A 'construct' event reports newraft_returned and, when the constructor returned, its last applied index, queued FSM batches and the observed FSM mutation channel capacity. Modes run in order replay_off, replay_on; the probe FSM discards applied entries and accepts the snapshot bytes.

comparisons.description: With the replay enabled, construction should return within the observation window.

scope.description: One node (LocalID A) constructed in four configurations from per-mode in-memory stores: a version-1 snapshot at index 1000 with configuration {A} plus committed LogCommand entries above it, with the commit-tracking store reporting the log's last index as commit index. assumptions: The fixture (snapshot, entries, staged commit index) is supplied by the harness; it is the restart shape a node that ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled can reach, with the commit index persisted atomically with the entries by the store contract.
Batches are derived as ceil(entries above the snapshot / MaxAppendEntries) and emitted as an operand rather than asserted from a constant.

The feature-on instance that does not return cannot be shut down; its goroutine is abandoned when the test process exits.
excluded: No on-disk store, no live cluster and no crash path is exercised.
The stalled constructor is not resumed and no timeout or external supervision is modelled.
No repository test was executed.

scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster whose node A restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} long enough for both sides to elect and commit a different entry at the same index and term, and is then healed; this revision samples each node's applied FSM commands after healing in addition to the log payloads.

basis.prefix: The harness builds five InmemTransports (A..E) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, starts A, B and C with MockFSM and Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true, waits for a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, waits on a Barrier and takes a user snapshot on A. scope.description: Real 5-node in-memory cluster in which node A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change newer than its snapshot, splits {A,C} from {B,D,E} so both sides commit at the same index and term, is healed, and is then repaired by forcing a snapshot install from a current-configuration leader while A is temporarily unreachable.

The repair phase records rather than asserts which current-configuration node leads: leadership is transferred to B only if the healed leader is not a current-configuration node.

The harness is a revision of the one used for the split-brain and applied-state experiments (adding the repair phase and TrailingLogs 0); the earlier comparisons remain recorded with those experiments' own receipts.
excluded: No user Restore, no compaction without a lagging follower and no term-changing truncation is exercised; only the snapshot-install path is.

comparisons.description: The ordinary recovery path should engage once the stale node falls behind a compacted leader: the node installs a snapshot.

The divergent entry at the conflict index should be gone from the restarted node's log after the install.

Negative half of the answer: a node that stayed up to date is not repaired by another node's snapshot install, so the cluster's applied state should still differ.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes, and the trigger is operationally realistic rather than harness-arranged. At the default batch size the requirement is 8193 entries, just above the default SnapshotThreshold, so a node needs failing or delayed snapshots to reach it - both are now observed (receipt e0d98aadc54b461792883fc8a2a82676 for delay, 49444692e9db40dd84b1aa3c6d603193 for failure), with the supplied-store receipts 00386ad8ea534d91a0ef7506fabc9527 giving the two-scale controls. interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate is that a node restarted with the feature rebuilds its membership from the configuration entry in its log even when it has no snapshot; the witness contradicts it in both forms. Admission index 0 records the fixture: cluster {A,B,C} with B leading, node A holding zero snapshots, a staged commit index of 11 over a log ending at 12, and A reporting {A,B,C} while running. After A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs (event index 1) it returns, replays to index 13, and reports an empty configuration - neither the id list nor the server count matches the bootstrap membership (comparisons 0 and 1 violated). The control restart without the feature (event index 2) reports {A,B,C} with three servers (comparisons 2 and 3 hold). Mechanism: the scan starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, restoreFromCommittedLogs has already raised lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 724-753, raft.go 1296-1363), and with no snapshot lastSnapshotIndex is zero, so every configuration entry in the log lies below the scan start and processConfigurationLogEntry is never called (api.go 610-620); the FSM replay still consumes those entries as ordinary commits. Consequences derived from source, not executed here: with latestIndex zero the node's heartbeat timeout logs 'no known peers, aborting election' and never transitions to candidate (raft.go 225-246), and its vote handling skips the membership check for an empty configuration, so it grants votes to candidates it does not know (raft.go 1660-1680). Limits: the observation is a construction state with a 300ms settle, in-memory stores with scaled timeouts, a graceful shutdown, and the node held no snapshots because the harness never took one rather than because of a store failure; the election and vote behaviours remain source-derived.
counterevidence: The identical restart without the feature rebuilds {A,B,C}, so the empty configuration is not a property of the stores or of the restart procedure.
The node's FSM did replay the log to index 13, so the empty configuration is not explained by missing log entries.
limitations: The empty configuration is observed at construction; the node's subsequent refusal to campaign and its vote grants are derived from source, not executed.
The absence of snapshots is arranged by the harness (ten-minute interval, none taken) rather than caused by a store failure.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown; one run per mode.

interpretations.rationale: This experiment characterises containment rather than a defect, and its predicates are all satisfied. Admission index 0 records the fixture (no snapshots on A, ten committed commands, A reporting {A,B,C} while running). After the feature-enabled restart, isolating the node from every peer for one second - twenty heartbeat timeouts at the configured 50ms - left it a follower that never entered candidate or leader state, with zero configured servers (comparisons 0 and 1 hold at index 2). The control restart, holding three configured servers, became a candidate during the same isolation (comparisons 2 and 3 hold at index 4), so the isolation is a real trigger and the empty configuration is what keeps the feature-enabled node from campaigning. Both nodes kept their term across the window (3 to 3, operands at indices 2 and 4), which the pre-vote extension explains: a candidate runs a pre-vote before incrementing its term, so the control could be observed in candidate state without a term change. Limits: the observation is a 1-second sample every 5ms in one run per mode, no votes were solicited from real peers, and the fault injected is transport disconnection only.
counterevidence: The control's candidate state shows the isolation would produce campaigning if a configuration were present, so the feature-enabled node's silence is attributable to the empty configuration.
The unchanged terms in both modes show the term operand must not be read as evidence of campaigning either way, given pre-vote.
limitations: One second of sampling per mode, no repetition across schedules.
No votes are solicited, so no election outcome is executed for either mode.
Transport disconnection is the only fault; no crash or store failure is involved.

They are compatible because both observe the same cluster identity, the same restart procedure (same stores, same leader B, ten committed commands, no snapshot on A) and the same two resulting configurations (empty for the feature-enabled restart, {A,B,C} for the control); each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.

interpretations.rationale: This experiment asserts the defect and every declared predicate held. The fixture admission carries A with no snapshots, ten committed commands and the live configuration {A,B,C} (index 0). While A still holds that configuration and knows no leader, the probe sent on behalf of identity P - absent from the configuration - is refused (comparison 0, index 2), and the refusal is attributable to membership rather than to timing or log age, because the request carried a term one above A's and a last log entry equal to A's and the event records that no leader was known (comparison 1). After the restart with the feature, A reports no servers while its log still records {A,B,C} and its last applied index is 13 (index 3); isolated again it still never campaigns, and the identical probe is now granted with A adopting the probe term (comparison 2, index 4). The real outside node X, whose log is a copy of A's with the bootstrap configuration entry replaced by {A,X}, then reaches leader state with A as its only voter partner (comparison 3), A follows it (comparison 4), A's log still names the committed {A,B,C} (comparison 5) and the cluster's own leader B keeps its leadership at the same time (comparison 6), all read at index 5.
counterevidence: A's own election gate still refuses to campaign while its configuration is empty, so the node never becomes a candidate itself; the defect is in the authority it grants, not in its own transition.

The grant is not explained by the node's state: in the control the node was a candidate and refused, and the node that granted was a follower, so the two outcomes differ with the configuration rather than with the state.
The outsider needs a reachable voter partner: with X's configuration {A,X} its quorum is two, so the election is only completed because the emptied node supplies the second vote.
limitations: The outsider's stores are supplied by the harness, so the scenario models a node whose stored configuration {A,X} was never this cluster's; the same reachability arises for a server reinstated from an older deployment or a recycled address.
Single sample per phase with in-memory transports and stores at scaled 50ms timeouts; each isolation window is 1.2s, twenty heartbeat timeouts, and the state is sampled every 5ms.
The two sides stay partitioned during the probes, so no write is applied by both leaders and the concurrent-commit consequence is not executed here.
Both probes are hand-built vote requests carrying the target's own last log entry, so they test the admission branch rather than what an out-of-date candidate would experience.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: a node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs while it holds no snapshot comes up with an empty configuration, and that empty configuration is not merely inert - the node refuses to campaign itself but still grants its vote to candidates it cannot see, which is enough to elect a leader its own committed configuration excludes. Receipts bdf2837a4c004f95b6c9b19db4fb8154 (the two restarts: empty with the feature, {A,B,C} without it) and d2973ec8cc524a9089c63dd046e1a4ff (the same restarts under isolation: no campaigning with the empty configuration, candidate state for the control) establish the configuration outcome and the gate. Receipt 1fb8595fb8664713a0dff87236bde04a adds the admission side: the same node, isolated and knowing no leader, refuses the outside candidacy while it holds {A,B,C} (index 2) and grants the identical request once the restart has left it with no servers (index 4); the outside node X, whose log records {A,X} and whose only voter partner is the emptied node, then reaches leader state at term 5 while the emptied node follows it with its log still committing {A,B,C} and the cluster's leader B keeps its leadership (index 5). Mechanism: the scan starting at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 combined with the replay that raises lastApplied past the configuration entry leaves latest empty, the election gate then blocks campaigning while latestIndex is zero (raft.go 225-246), and the membership guard in requestVote is conditional on a non-empty server list (raft.go 1656-1680), so the emptied node admits and grants a vote it would otherwise refuse. Scope of the consequence: the vote is bounded by the log up-to-dateness rule and by the candidate's own quorum, so the defect yields one extra authority grant rather than unrestricted admission, and the node's participation resumes as soon as the cluster installs a snapshot or a configuration entry reaches it.

045d23497a8a47e79cccfb8361d0d6b9-gap-0.explanation: Yes to both.
